title: 🏅 Full Mock Test

sections.heading: Full Mock Test
sections.body:
This lesson links to a full IELTS mock test.

Practise all four sections under realistic exam conditions:
• 🎧 Listening — audio plays once (Chrome TTS)
• 👁️ Reading — full passages with T/F/NG, MCQ, headings
• ✍️ Writing — Task 1 + Task 2 with word counter
• 🗣️ Speaking — cue cards + timers + Band 9 tips

sections.heading: Before you start
sections.body:
Find a quiet place.
Have a pencil and paper ready.
Set aside ~85 minutes for a full test.
Turn off all notifications.

highlight: Mock tests are the single most effective exam preparation strategy. Complete at least 2 full tests before your exam day.

question: When should you take full mock tests in your preparation?
options: Only on the day before the exam
Regularly from mid-preparation, at least 2–3 weeks before the exam
correct: Regularly from mid-preparation, at least 2–3 weeks before the exam
explanation:
Mock tests serve several purposes:
• Identify weaknesses to focus on
• Build exam stamina (3 hours is tiring)
• Practise time management
• Reduce exam anxiety through familiarity

Doing them TOO early is also fine — they diagnose exactly where to focus.

question: After a mock test, what is the MOST important thing to do?
options: Forget about it and move on
Carefully review every wrong answer and understand WHY it was wrong
correct: Carefully review every wrong answer and understand WHY it was wrong
explanation:
Review is where the real learning happens.

For each wrong answer ask:
• WHY was my answer wrong?
• What key information did I miss?
• What trap did I fall for?
• How do I recognise this trap next time?

Without review, mock tests are just practice without learning.
